newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on crop talk, China rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on crop talk, China rumors.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on talk of better-than-expected yields per acre in the U.S. soybean harvest areas plus China rumors, traders said.
"The rumors are that China reneged on bean purchases, rumors the letters of credit didn't come through," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Commercial selling, led by Continental Grain's sale of 15.0 million bushels of November, led to the China talk, the traders said.
The U.S. Midwest soybean harvest was nearing the half-way mark by Sunday and producers were reporting good yields.

"We're seeing yields mostly in the mid-40s to mid-50s (bushels per acre)," said Fred Gent, grain manager at McLean County Service Co in Bloomington, Ill. "I don't think we expected quite that good but that's about average for us."

A continuation of the technical slide also was noted, traders said, with technical indicators staying bearish with the key moving averages weighing on prices. But the nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November indicated a short term oversold scenario and closed at 17.768 points.
Soybeans closed 2-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with November down 2-1/2 at $6.88-1/2.
An RSI of 20 or less is generally perceived as a barometer of an oversold market for the near term.
Traders said November appears stuck in a trading range with the low $6.80 per bushel a support area and stiff resistance was seen at $7.00.
"There's support in the low 80s in corn and beans. That's where the support was before and that's where it held today," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Soybeans were underpinned by damper and cooler weather in the U.S. Midwest which was expected to slow combining of the soybean crop.
"The weather is still a little supportive and the six- to 10-day was a little friendly with the moisture prospects," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 54,000 contracts, down from 60,107 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Continental Grain bought 400 January $6.50 puts at three to 3-1/4 cents, Produce Grain bought 400 November $6.75 puts at 1-7/8 to two cents and Continental Grain bought 400 March $6.50 puts at 4-3/4 to five cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 21,500 contracts, down from 22,435 Wednesday.
